# WO-2026-08-09-B15-03 — the truthful Terra binding
# guidance: WO-YYYY-MM-DD-nn — slice title

## Acceptance criteria

**Warwick ruled option B on 2026-08-09.** His words, which are the specification:

> *"I chose bounded Terra deliberately for natural-language shopping-answer interpretation. Do NOT substitute `reason` because it is easier to reach. Do NOT widen the durable vocabulary so `reason` can become acceptable after the fact."*

**AC1 — establish the binding, do not assume it.** He is explicit: *"Do NOT silently assume `fusion.query == gpt-5.6-terra`."* `ROLE_ALIAS.query` resolves to `process.env.FUSION_MODEL_QUERY || 'fusion.query'`, and `config.mjs:36` claims in a comment that the box maps *"query gpt-5.6-terra"*. **That comment is evidence, not proof** — the mapping lives on the gateway, outside this repo. Establish what you can from the repo and environment, and **state plainly what remains configuration truth on the box** rather than asserting it.

**AC2 — export a gateway-only role function, following the `vision()` precedent exactly.** `vision()` in `models.mjs` is already the right shape and its comment already argues the case: it has **deliberately NO fallback**, because handing a blind text model a prompt about an image it cannot see would *"invite an invented answer — exactly the failure mode a household shopping list must never have."* **A free-text shopping answer is the same case.** So the answer path must reach the gateway and **throw** where no gateway is configured — never `lightrag`. Use the existing role abstraction; **do not create a second credential or model path.**

**AC3 — bind the answer interpreter to it.** The grounding contract, the allowed-id set, the FK guard and the `clarification_required` degradations all stay **exactly as you built them**. This is a change of which model answers, not of how it is bounded.

**AC4 — provenance becomes TRUE.** `interpreted_by` stays `'terra'` — **migration 017 is NOT touched.** `interpreted_model` must record **the alias actually invoked, resolved at call time**, so that if the box maps it elsewhere the row shows what really answered. Warwick: *"model/alias evidence identifies what was actually invoked, not what we hoped was invoked."*

**AC5 — the discriminating proof.** A test must go **RED if the answer binding is switched back to `reason`**, and GREEN when Terra is restored. Demonstrate that mutation in your handback. Also prove, per his list: production `createDeps()` binds the real interpreter with **no** test override · free text reaches the Terra-bound path · `reason()` is **not** the answer interpreter path · no gateway cannot fall back to LightRAG · a deterministic button still spends **zero** model calls · an out-of-grounding product id becomes `clarification_required`, never a decision · persisted provenance agrees with the path actually invoked.

**No fake may be capable of satisfying the production-wiring assertion** — your `productionWiring.test.js` already meets that bar; keep it.
# guidance: each independently checkable. If automatic, no AC may be satisfiable by a manual invocation of the delivered script alone.

## Sequencing

**Immediate. This is the only thing standing between Gate 1 and PASS.**

**One correction to carry in your handback, not to investigate.** Veritas established that a shop which cannot interpret **never reaches `AWAIT_LINE_RESOLUTION`** — `clarification_required` opens a real round-2 question, so the gate takes its ordinary `NEEDS_DECISION` branch and D-2's card never fires there. Visibility on that path comes from the older `runtime.js queueShopCards`. **D-2 is still correct and stays implemented for the actual park.** Larry's earlier explanation was wrong and is being corrected in the record; **do not turn this into an investigation.**

Short read-back confirming the order is buildable and naming anything genuinely unsettled — especially if you find `fusion.query` is **not** bound to Terra on the box, which is the one discovery that changes the shape of this work. Then build.
